findings.description: The reports_archive bucket stores vendor data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are written without default SSE and are unencrypted at rest (or rely only on weak SSE-S3 defaults with no KMS key).
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is attached, so the bucket can be made public and its contents (vendor roster and reports) exposed.
The ledger_exports bucket contains financial ledger exports but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger bucket, so overwritten or deleted financial records cannot be recovered to detect or investigate tampering.
model_artifacts has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
The ops_runbooks bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving operational runbook content unencrypted at rest.

audit_trail uses acl = "log-delivery-write", a canned ACL that grants the S3 log-delivery group write and read-ACP permissions to the audit bucket, broadening access beyond intended principals on a security-relevant log store.

findings.issue_category: sensitive object uploaded without KMS encryption
findings.description: The reports_seed_object uploads vendor-roster.xlsx into reports_archive with no kms_key_id or server-side encryption arguments, so this vendor data object is stored unencrypted at rest.
